learning_outcomes.text: Masters fundamental concepts regarding main forms of energy.
Knows methods of energy production and utilization.
Understands the necessity of preparing energy balances and their classification.
Masters general principles for preparing energy balances and their methodology.
Knows ways to assess the energy efficiency of energy-consuming processes.
Knows the characteristics of energy audit and its types.
Knows the phases of a complete audit and its logical execution scheme.
Knows the specific tools of the energy auditor.
Knows how to prepare an audit report.
Uses digital instruments for processing experimental data.
Masters experimental procedures for collecting measurement data on various thermal systems.
Operates measurement equipment used in energy auditing.
Is capable of proposing solutions to improve and mitigate disadvantages identified in the audit process.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the timely and correct execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group, applies relational and efficient teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents oneself in their field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.
Develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introductory concepts: Energy. Forms of energy. Energy production and utilization. Energy efficiency. Generalities. Definitions. Energy balance and energy audit. Energy management. National Energy Regulatory Authority (ANRE).

Energy balance: Generalities. Definitions. Classification of balances. General principles for preparing energy balances. Main types of energy balances. General methodological guidelines for preparing energy balances. Assessing the energy efficiency of energy-consuming processes.
Energy strategies: Introduction. Organizational structure. Energy policies. Planning.
Energy audit: Introduction. Types of energy audit. Preliminary audit. Phases of a complete audit and its logical execution scheme. Tools of the energy auditor. Audit report.
Presentation of the design theme and assignment of initial data
Preparation of the energy balance for the components of the installation (building)
Preparation of the energy balance for the entire installation (building)
Development of measures and recommendations for energy saving

assessment_methods.method: Exam / Verification (includes systematic observation, individual/team assignments, report/case study, formative evaluation test, summative evaluation test)
Project (includes project activity, project completion, project defense)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is determined by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
